meta.description: Batch program that reads daily credit card transactions and validates each transaction by verifying the card number and resolving it to a customer account, as a precursor to posting.
meta.process_description: The program sequentially reads all transactions from the daily transaction file and, for each transaction, performs a two-step lookup: first it uses the card number to find the corresponding account and customer via a cross-reference file, then it retrieves the full account record from the account master file. Transactions where the card number cannot be found in the cross-reference are flagged and skipped, while transactions where the resolved account cannot be found in the account file are also flagged. The program appears to be an earlier or lighter version of CBTRN02C, focused on the validation and lookup phase rather than the full posting of balances — it opens the transaction posting file but does not appear to write to it in the visible code. All files are opened in read-only (INPUT) mode, suggesting this may be a validation/reconciliation pass rather than a full posting run.

files.DALYTRAN: Daily transaction file — the source file containing all credit card transactions to be processed for the day
files.CUSTFILE: Customer master file — holds customer demographic and profile records, referenced by customer ID
files.XREFFILE: Card-to-account cross-reference file — maps a credit card number to its associated account ID and customer ID
files.CARDFILE: Card master file — holds credit card records including card status and attributes
files.ACCTFILE: Account master file — holds credit card account records including balances and credit limits
files.TRANFILE: Transaction history file — the indexed file where validated/posted transactions are stored as permanent records

business_rules: Every transaction must have a valid, recognisable card number — if the card number cannot be found in the cross-reference file, the transaction is skipped and not posted
Every card number must resolve to a valid, existing account — if the account cannot be found in the account master file, the transaction is flagged with an error message
Transactions are processed strictly in the sequential order they appear in the daily transaction file — no sorting or prioritisation is applied
Any file I/O error (other than end-of-file) on the daily transaction file causes an immediate abnormal termination (abend) of the program, protecting data integrity
The card-to-account cross-reference is the authoritative source for linking a card number to an account and customer — the card number alone is not sufficient to identify an account

variables.name: FD-TRAN-RECORD
variables.description: File buffer record for the transaction history file (TRANFILE). Represents the physical layout of a posted transaction record as it is written to permanent storage. Acts as the I/O bridge between working storage and the on-disk transaction history.

variables.name: FD-TRAN-ID
variables.description: The unique transaction identifier in the transaction history file record. Serves as the indexed key that allows a specific posted transaction to be retrieved from the permanent transaction history file.

variables.name: FD-CUST-DATA
variables.description: The remaining payload of the transaction history file record beyond the transaction ID. Contains all other transaction details (type, amount, merchant, card number, timestamps, etc.) as a raw block, completing the 350-byte transaction record layout.

variables.name: FD-CUSTFILE-REC
variables.description: File buffer record for the customer master file (CUSTFILE). Represents the physical layout of a customer record as read from disk, providing the I/O bridge to access cardholder demographic and profile information.

variables.name: FD-CUST-ID
variables.description: The unique customer identifier in the customer master file record. Serves as the indexed key used to locate a specific cardholder's profile record when verifying the customer associated with a transaction.

variables.name: FD-CUST-DATA
variables.description: The remaining payload of the customer master file record beyond the customer ID. Contains all other customer details (name, address, SSN, FICO score, etc.) as a raw block, completing the 500-byte customer record layout.

variables.name: FD-XREFFILE-REC
variables.description: File buffer record for the card-to-account cross-reference file (XREFFILE). Represents the physical layout of a cross-reference record as read from disk, enabling the program to map a credit card number to its associated account and customer.

variables.name: FD-XREF-CARD-NUM
variables.description: The credit card number as stored in the cross-reference file record. Serves as the indexed key used to look up which account and customer a given card number belongs to — the primary linkage between a transaction's card number and the cardholder's account.

variables.name: FD-XREF-DATA
variables.description: The remaining payload of the cross-reference file record beyond the card number. Contains the associated customer ID and account ID as a raw block, completing the 50-byte cross-reference record layout.

variables.name: FD-CARDFILE-REC
variables.description: File buffer record for the card master file (CARDFILE). Represents the physical layout of a credit card record as read from disk, providing the I/O bridge to access card-level attributes such as status, CVV, and expiration date.

variables.name: FD-CARD-NUM
variables.description: The credit card number as stored in the card master file record. Serves as the indexed key used to retrieve the full card record, enabling validation of card-level attributes (e.g., active status, expiration) for a transaction being processed.

variables.name: FD-CARD-DATA
variables.description: The remaining payload of the card master file record beyond the card number. Contains all other card attributes (account ID, CVV, embossed name, expiration date, active status, etc.) as a raw block, completing the 150-byte card record layout.

variables.name: FD-ACCTFILE-REC
variables.description: File buffer record for the account master file (ACCTFILE). Represents the physical layout of a credit card account record as read from disk, providing the I/O bridge to access account balances, credit limits, and account status.

variables.name: FD-ACCT-ID
variables.description: The unique account identifier in the account master file record. Serves as the indexed key used to retrieve the full account record for a cardholder, enabling verification that the account resolved from the cross-reference actually exists and is accessible.

variables.name: FD-ACCT-DATA
variables.description: The remaining payload of the account master file record beyond the account ID. Contains all other account details (balance, credit limit, status, dates, etc.) as a raw block, completing the 300-byte account record layout.

variables.name: FD-TRANFILE-REC
variables.description: File buffer record for the transaction history output file (TRANFILE). Represents the physical layout of a validated transaction record as it is written to the permanent transaction history, completing the posting process for each successfully validated transaction.

variables.name: FD-TRANS-ID
variables.description: The unique transaction identifier written to the transaction history file. Acts as the indexed key for the posted transaction record, enabling future retrieval of any specific transaction from the permanent history.

variables.name: FD-ACCT-DATA
variables.description: The remaining payload of the transaction history output record beyond the transaction ID. Contains all other transaction details (type, amount, merchant, card number, timestamps, etc.) as a raw block, completing the 350-byte posted transaction record layout.

variables.name: DALYTRAN-STATUS
variables.description: The two-character file status code returned by the operating system after every I/O operation on the daily transaction file (DALYTRAN). Used to determine whether each read succeeded, reached end-of-file, or encountered an error that would require aborting the batch run.

variables.name: DALYTRAN-STAT1
variables.description: The first (major) character of the daily transaction file status code. A value of '0' indicates a successful read; '1' indicates end-of-file has been reached, signalling that all transactions for the day have been processed.

variables.name: DALYTRAN-STAT2
variables.description: The second (minor) character of the daily transaction file status code. Provides additional detail about the outcome of the I/O operation on the daily transaction file, used together with DALYTRAN-STAT1 to diagnose specific error conditions.

variables.name: CUSTFILE-STATUS
variables.description: The two-character file status code returned after every I/O operation on the customer master file (CUSTFILE). Used to confirm whether a customer record was successfully retrieved or whether an error occurred during the customer lookup.

variables.name: CUSTFILE-STAT1
variables.description: The first (major) character of the customer master file status code. A value of '0' indicates the customer record was found and read successfully; other values indicate the customer could not be located or an I/O error occurred.

variables.name: CUSTFILE-STAT2
variables.description: The second (minor) character of the customer master file status code. Provides supplementary detail about the result of the customer file I/O operation, used together with CUSTFILE-STAT1 for precise error diagnosis.

variables.name: XREFFILE-STATUS
variables.description: The two-character file status code returned after every I/O operation on the card-to-account cross-reference file (XREFFILE). Critical for determining whether a transaction's card number was successfully resolved to an account — a failed lookup means the transaction must be skipped.

variables.name: XREFFILE-STAT1
variables.description: The first (major) character of the cross-reference file status code. A value of '0' means the card number was found and the account/customer linkage was successfully resolved; other values indicate the card number is unrecognised and the transaction cannot be posted.

variables.name: XREFFILE-STAT2
variables.description: The second (minor) character of the cross-reference file status code. Provides additional detail about the cross-reference lookup result, used together with XREFFILE-STAT1 to distinguish between 'not found' and other error conditions.

variables.name: CARDFILE-STATUS
variables.description: The two-character file status code returned after every I/O operation on the card master file (CARDFILE). Used to confirm whether a card record was successfully retrieved when validating card-level attributes for a transaction.

variables.name: CARDFILE-STAT1
variables.description: The first (major) character of the card master file status code. A value of '0' indicates the card record was found and read successfully; other values indicate the card could not be located or an I/O error occurred during card validation.

variables.name: CARDFILE-STAT2
variables.description: The second (minor) character of the card master file status code. Provides supplementary detail about the card file I/O result, used together with CARDFILE-STAT1 for precise error diagnosis during card validation.

variables.name: ACCTFILE-STATUS
variables.description: The two-character file status code returned after every I/O operation on the account master file (ACCTFILE). Used to verify whether the account resolved from the cross-reference actually exists in the account master — a failed lookup means the transaction cannot be posted.

variables.name: ACCTFILE-STAT1
variables.description: The first (major) character of the account master file status code. A value of '0' means the account record was found and retrieved successfully; other values indicate the account does not exist or an I/O error occurred, triggering an error message for the transaction.

variables.name: ACCTFILE-STAT2
variables.description: The second (minor) character of the account master file status code. Provides additional detail about the account lookup result, used together with ACCTFILE-STAT1 to distinguish between 'account not found' and other error conditions.

variables.name: TRANFILE-STATUS
variables.description: The two-character file status code returned after every I/O operation on the transaction history output file (TRANFILE). Used to confirm whether a validated transaction was successfully written to the permanent transaction history.

variables.name: TRANFILE-STAT1
variables.description: The first (major) character of the transaction history file status code. A value of '0' confirms the transaction was successfully posted to the permanent history file; other values indicate a write failure that would need to be investigated.

variables.name: TRANFILE-STAT2
variables.description: The second (minor) character of the transaction history file status code. Provides supplementary detail about the write operation result, used together with TRANFILE-STAT1 for precise diagnosis of any posting failure.

variables.name: IO-STATUS
variables.description: A general-purpose two-character I/O status holder used to capture and evaluate file operation results in a centralised error-handling routine. Consolidates status codes from any file into a single location for uniform error reporting and abend decisions.

variables.name: IO-STAT1
variables.description: The first (major) character of the general I/O status code. Used in the centralised error handler to determine the broad category of any file operation failure across all files in the batch program.

variables.name: IO-STAT2
variables.description: The second (minor) character of the general I/O status code. Provides additional detail to the centralised error handler, enabling precise identification of the specific I/O error condition that occurred.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-BINARY
variables.description: A two-byte binary work field used to convert a two-character file status code into a numeric value. Enables the program to perform arithmetic comparisons on I/O status codes for error evaluation and abend code generation.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-ALPHA
variables.description: An alphanumeric overlay of the TWO-BYTES-BINARY field. Allows the same two bytes of memory to be read as individual characters, so that a file status code (two characters) can be loaded into the binary field and then interpreted numerically for error handling.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-LEFT
variables.description: The left (first) character byte of the two-byte status conversion field. Receives the first character of a file status code so it can be combined with the right byte and interpreted as a binary number for error code processing.

variables.name: TWO-BYTES-RIGHT
variables.description: The right (second) character byte of the two-byte status conversion field. Receives the second character of a file status code so it can be combined with the left byte and interpreted as a binary number for error code processing.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-04
variables.description: A structured work area used to decompose and display a numeric I/O status code in a human-readable format for error reporting. Splits the status number into a single leading digit and a three-digit remainder to facilitate formatted error messages.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-0401
variables.description: The leading single digit of the formatted I/O error status code. Represents the major category digit of the file status for inclusion in error messages, helping operations staff identify the class of I/O failure that caused a batch abend.

variables.name: IO-STATUS-0403
variables.description: The three-digit minor portion of the formatted I/O error status code. Represents the detailed sub-code of the file status for inclusion in error messages, providing operations staff with the specific error detail needed to diagnose and resolve a batch failure.

variables.name: APPL-RESULT
variables.description: A numeric result code that captures the outcome of key processing steps within the batch run. Acts as a central indicator of whether the program is proceeding normally, has reached the end of the transaction file, or has encountered a condition requiring special handling.

variables.name: APPL-AOK
variables.description: A condition name that evaluates to true when the last processing step completed successfully (result code = 0). Used as a readable business condition to confirm that a transaction read or validation step proceeded without error.

variables.name: APPL-EOF
variables.description: A condition name that evaluates to true when the end of the daily transaction file has been reached (result code = 16). Signals that all transactions for the day have been read and the batch processing loop should terminate normally.

variables.name: END-OF-DAILY-TRANS-FILE
variables.description: A processing control flag that tracks whether all daily transactions have been read. Initialised to 'N' (not finished) at the start of the batch run and set to 'Y' when the end of the daily transaction file is reached, causing the main processing loop to stop and end-of-day wrap-up to begin.

variables.name: ABCODE
variables.description: The abnormal termination (abend) code passed to the operating system when the batch program encounters a fatal error it cannot recover from, such as an unexpected I/O failure on the daily transaction file. Allows operations staff and job schedulers to identify the specific reason the batch job failed.

variables.name: TIMING
variables.description: A numeric work field used to capture or pass timing-related information during the batch run, typically used in conjunction with system service calls for performance measurement or elapsed-time tracking of the batch transaction processing job.

variables.name: WS-MISC-VARIABLES
variables.description: A working-storage group containing miscellaneous status indicators used during transaction validation. Holds the results of the two critical lookups — the card-to-account cross-reference and the account master retrieval — that determine whether each transaction can be posted.

variables.name: WS-XREF-READ-STATUS
variables.description: Records whether the card number on a transaction was successfully found in the card-to-account cross-reference file. A value of 0 means the card number is recognised and has been linked to an account and customer; a value of 4 means the card number is unknown and the transaction must be skipped and not posted.

variables.name: WS-ACCT-READ-STATUS
variables.description: Records whether the account identified through the cross-reference lookup was successfully retrieved from the account master file. A value of 0 confirms the account exists and its details are available for posting; a value of 4 means the account record is missing, triggering an error message and preventing the transaction from being posted.

paragraphs.name: MAIN-PARA
paragraphs.description: MAIN-PARA is the master orchestration routine for the daily transaction validation batch run. It opens all required files, drives a sequential loop that validates every transaction's card number and resolves it to a live account, then closes all files and terminates cleanly.

paragraphs.name: 1000-DALYTRAN-GET-NEXT
paragraphs.description: This paragraph advances the batch process by reading the next credit card transaction from the daily transaction file, then evaluates the outcome to either continue processing, signal that all transactions have been consumed, or halt the entire batch run if an unexpected file error occurs.

paragraphs.name: 2000-LOOKUP-XREF
paragraphs.description: This paragraph performs the authoritative lookup that links a credit card number to its owning account and customer by querying the card-to-account cross-reference file. It is the critical validation gate that determines whether a transaction can proceed to posting or must be skipped.

paragraphs.name: 3000-READ-ACCOUNT
paragraphs.description: Retrieves the full account record from the account master file using the account ID resolved from the card cross-reference lookup. If the account cannot be found, the transaction is flagged as invalid and will not be posted.

paragraphs.name: 0000-DALYTRAN-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the daily credit card transaction file in preparation for the batch validation run. If the file cannot be opened successfully, the program immediately halts to prevent any processing against an unavailable or corrupt transaction source.

paragraphs.name: 0100-CUSTFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the customer master file so that customer profile data is available for transaction validation. If the file cannot be opened, the batch run is immediately aborted to prevent processing transactions without access to customer records.

paragraphs.name: 0200-XREFFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the card-to-account cross-reference file in preparation for transaction validation. It is a critical startup step — if the cross-reference file cannot be opened, the entire batch run is immediately aborted, since no transaction can be validated without it.

paragraphs.name: 0300-CARDFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the credit card master file so that card records can be read during transaction validation. If the file cannot be opened, the batch run is immediately aborted to prevent processing transactions without access to card data.

paragraphs.name: 0400-ACCTFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: Opens the account master file so that account records can be retrieved and validated during transaction processing. If the file cannot be opened, the batch run is immediately aborted to prevent processing transactions against an inaccessible or potentially corrupt account store.

paragraphs.name: 0500-TRANFILE-OPEN
paragraphs.description: This paragraph opens the transaction history file in preparation for the batch run, ensuring the permanent transaction store is accessible before processing begins. If the file cannot be opened, the program halts immediately to prevent any processing against an unavailable or corrupt transaction store.

paragraphs.name: 9000-DALYTRAN-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph closes the daily transaction file at the end of the batch run, ensuring all file resources are properly released. If the file cannot be closed cleanly, the program raises a critical error and terminates abnormally to protect data integrity.

paragraphs.name: 9100-CUSTFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the customer master file at the end of batch processing, ensuring all file resources are properly released. If the file cannot be closed cleanly, the program raises a critical error and halts immediately to protect data integrity.

paragraphs.name: 9200-XREFFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the card-to-account cross-reference file once all transaction lookups are complete, ensuring the file is properly released and terminating the program abnormally if the closure fails to protect data integrity.

paragraphs.name: 9300-CARDFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the credit card master file after all card lookups have been completed, ensuring the file is properly released. If the file cannot be closed cleanly, the program halts immediately to prevent data corruption or resource leaks.

paragraphs.name: 9400-ACCTFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: This paragraph safely closes the account master file at the end of the batch run, ensuring all file resources are properly released. If the file cannot be closed cleanly, the program raises a critical error and terminates immediately to protect data integrity.

paragraphs.name: 9500-TRANFILE-CLOSE
paragraphs.description: Closes the transaction history file at the end of the batch run, ensuring all file resources are properly released. If the file cannot be closed cleanly, the program raises a critical error and terminates abnormally to protect data integrity.

paragraphs.name: Z-ABEND-PROGRAM
paragraphs.description: This paragraph performs an immediate, controlled abnormal termination of the batch program when a critical, unrecoverable error is detected. It ensures the failure is clearly signalled to the operations team and the job scheduler, preventing any further processing that could compromise data integrity.

paragraphs.name: Z-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS
paragraphs.description: This paragraph formats and displays a human-readable file status code to the system log whenever a file I/O operation produces an error, supporting operator diagnosis and audit of file processing failures during the batch run.
